title: Should Christian wives take their husband’s last name? | Institute for Family Studies
gist: Truncated Christian Post teaser, carried by IFS, opening a debate on whether Christian wives should take their husband's surname, starting from Lucy Stone's 1855 refusal; no argument or data in the excerpt.

insights.claim: The Christian Post piece (excerpted by IFS) frames women keeping their surnames at marriage as a feminist act starting with suffragist Lucy Stone in 1855, later followed by suffragists, actresses, executives and many third-wave feminists, and asks whether Christian wives should take their husband's name.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Only a teaser; it signals cultural debate over marital naming conventions but gives no data or conclusion.
insights.locator: In 1855, a suffragist named Lucy Stone
